Best Family Vacation Destinations in California

By Marcus Webb · March 18, 2026 · Updated August 22, 2026

California is the destination families reach for when one theme park trip isn’t quite enough, or when the plan is a proper road trip rather than a single home base. That flexibility is the appeal — and also the thing that trips people up when they try to fit too much of the state into too short a trip.

This guide breaks the state into the regions that actually make sense to base a family trip around, with an honest read on which is the best fit depending on your kids’ ages and how much driving you’re willing to do.

Why California works so well for families

California's real advantage isn't any single attraction — it's the range packed into one state. A family can do theme parks in Anaheim, redwoods in the north, and a beach town in between, without ever needing a connecting flight. That's rare.

The trade-off is distance. California looks compact on a map of the US but Los Angeles to San Francisco is a six-hour drive, and trying to cover the whole state in one trip is the most common planning mistake we see. Pick a region and go deep instead.

Best areas to base a trip

Anaheim & Orange County

Disneyland and California Adventure are the draw, but Orange County's beach towns — Huntington Beach, Laguna — make a good add-on for a day or two of decompression after the parks.

San Diego

The most consistently family-friendly city in the state. The zoo and Safari Park are genuinely worth the hype, the beaches are calmer than LA's, and the weather is the most reliable in California.

San Francisco Bay Area

Better for kids aged seven and up who can handle hills and public transit. The Exploratorium and a cable car ride are highlights; pair it with a day trip to the redwoods at Muir Woods.

Central Coast (Santa Barbara to Monterey)

The best pick for a slower, scenic-drive-style trip — aquariums, tide pools, and small towns that don't require a full itinerary to enjoy.

Things kids can do

  • Disneyland and Disney California Adventure, still the benchmark for a first big theme park trip
  • San Diego Zoo and Safari Park, both easily worth a full day each
  • Tide pooling at low tide anywhere along the Central Coast — free, and a reliable hit with kids 4+
  • Monterey Bay Aquarium, particularly strong for kids fascinated by sea otters and kelp forests
  • Redwood walks in Muir Woods or, further north, Redwood National Park for older kids

Travel tips

  • Don't try to combine Southern and Northern California in one trip unless you have two weeks — the drive alone eats a full day each way
  • Coastal fog ('June gloom') is common along the Central and Northern Coast in early summer mornings; pack layers even in July
  • Anaheim hotel prices swing hard with park calendar — a few days' shift in dates can meaningfully change the cost
  • Car seats are required by California law for children under 8 or under 4'9" — confirm your rental company provides them if you're flying in

Frequently asked questions

Is California too expensive for a family vacation?

It can be pricey in Anaheim and San Francisco specifically, but San Diego and the Central Coast have a wider range of mid-range family accommodation. Traveling shoulder season (April–June, September–October) also helps significantly.

How many days do you need for a California family trip?

For one region done properly — Anaheim plus a beach day, or San Diego on its own — five to seven days is comfortable. Trying to cover more than one region needs ten days or more.

Is Southern or Northern California better for young kids?

Southern California, generally — the weather is more reliable, San Diego and Anaheim are both built around family tourism, and driving distances between attractions are shorter.
